note: Romani bands first: Bihari-era recruiting pieces played by Hungarian Gypsy orchestras from the 1950s to today. Then the village verbunk of Szatmár, Rábaköz, Kapuvár, Gyimes and the Székely lands, played by village musicians and táncház bands. The Lakatos and Boross 1950s tracks are dated only '1954–1959' on the page, and the Capella Savaria disc has no date, so their years are left open.

size.basis: MusicBrainz alone lists about 60 recordings with verbunkos and about 75 with verbunk in the title (many of the verbunkos ones are Bartók's Contrasts), a small, uneven sample of a repertoire that Hungarian Romani restaurant bands (the Lakatos dynasty, the 100-member Budapest Gypsy orchestra), state folk ensembles, village bands and táncház groups have recorded since the 1950s, usually as one verbunk or verbunkos-and-friss per album; Bihari alone left 84 compositions that later bands still play. Range is a reasoned guess, not a catalogue count; core is what a Hungarian listener would call essential: the Bihari-Lavotta-Csermák pieces as played by the great Gypsy bands, plus the classic village verbunks (Szatmár, Rábaköz, Kapuvár, Vasvár, Gyimes, Székely).
